extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in mathematics and computer science (popular-science audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A popular-science explainer article (Abstractions blog / Quanta Magazine) introducing and interpreting the Curry–Howard correspondence for a general educated audience. Focuses on concept exposition and high-level implications for math and computer science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment moderation purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Quanta Magazine moderates comments to facilitate an informed, substantive, civil conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should contribute to an informed, substantive, and civil discussion. The statement frames moderation as enabling constructive conversation rather than open-ended publishing; posts failing to meet that goal risk removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Abusive, profane, self-promotional, misleading, incoherent or off-topic comments will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly disallowed categories are listed. Authors of comments should avoid abuse, profanity, self-promotion, misinformation, incoherence, and off-topic remarks. The list functions as a rejection checklist for moderators and a guidance checklist for commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation staffing / timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderators are staffed during regular business hours (New York time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because moderation is only staffed during NY business hours, posting may not yield immediate approval or response outside those times; enforcement and visibility depend on moderator availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Can only accept comments written in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be in English to be accepted; non-English comments are subject to rejection regardless of content. This is a hard submission requirement tied to moderation capacity and audience language.
